events.description: [vc_row][vc_column][ultimate_heading source="post_title" heading_tag="h1" main_heading_color="#BE1E2D" main_heading_font_family="font_family:|font_call:" main_heading_style="font-weight:bold;"][/ultimate_heading][ultimate_spacer height="10" height_on_tabs="10" height_on_tabs_portrait="10" height_on_mob_landscape="7" height_on_mob="7"][dt_fancy_separator separator_color="accent" line_thickness="3"][ultimate_spacer height="10" height_on_tabs="10" height_on_tabs_portrait="10" height_on_mob_landscape="7" height_on_mob="7"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][dt_fancy_image image_id="27337" onclick="lightbox" width="" caption="on"][ultimate_spacer height="32" height_on_tabs="32" height_on_tabs_portrait="32" height_on_mob_landscape="28" height_on_mob="28"][vc_column_text css=""]        Learn the highs and lows of queer history in Boston and Provincetown in this fascinating book talk!              Join author Russ López for an author talk centered around his work The Hub of the Gay Universe: An LGBTQ+ History of Boston, Provincetown, and Beyond.    Learn about the highs: the torrid romances of actress Charlotte Cushman, the glamorous nightlife of 1950s Boston, the great outpouring of happiness that accompanied the country's first same-sex marriages. Understand the tragedies: murders of trans women and gay men, the terrible waves of repression of the 1920s, and the devastation of the HIV/AIDS epidemic.    This talk is part of our programming related to our special exhibition Queer History West End, exclusively sponsored by Massachusetts LGBT Chamber of Commerce and Mass250. The exhibit was made in partnership with Queer History Boston. Stop by early and glance around the gallery to see the exhibit for yourself!    López is the author of six nonfiction books, the editor of LatineLit, and the writer of numerous essays. Originally from California, Russ has degrees from Stanford, Harvard, and Boston University. He splits his time between Boston and Ptown year-round.    Books will be available for purchase at the event. events.title: Hatha Yoga w/ Live Music
events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. 
 
 
 
 
    Reserve a spot
   
 
 
 
 
 
 (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

The  Toad Revival Series  is our tribute to the bands that built this stage, note by note, night after night. It’s a laid-back, early evening show filled with familiar sounds, longtime favorites, and the spirit of a scene that never really faded—just waited for the right time to plug back in. events.title: Tavern Crawl: A Dungeon and Dragons Inspired Fantasy Bar Crawl
events.description: A Themed Interactive Bar Crawl with Puzzles, Powers, and Poor Decisions hosted by  Incantrix Productions .  Tickets available here. Grab a drink. Choose a class. Save the day. This is no boring pub crawl, this is a  fully interactive, narrative-driven Dungeons & Dragons–inspired tavern crawl  where  you  are the heroes on your own personal adventure. You and your group will embark on a  2-hour quest  across  four themed locations , each run by live actors portraying important Guild members with problems they are looking to solve with your help. There are  no wrong answers —only consequences, alliances, and chaos. These adventures are designed by award-winning game and puzzle designers (and not AI) and a ton of real production experience with backgrounds from Disney, WB Games, and more! (No Willy Wonka disasters here!) 🧙 HOW IT WORKS Groups start every  20 minutes . Each group receives: Character cards A  one-time-use class power At each new location, you will meet fascinating NPCs who will present you with interesting dilemmas. You’ll solve puzzles, make choices, drink potions, argue philosophy, and possibly die. Yes.  Die. (Calm down death is not the end… or is it?!) You do not need to have a single previous experience with Dungeons or Dragons in order to fully enjoy this experience. You do not need a certificate in rules lawyering, there will be very few rules, and lots and lots of bawdy fun. 🧑‍🎭 CHOOSE YOUR CLASS Spellcaster (think; Wizard, Sorcerer, Hedge Mage) Fighter (think; Barbarian, Fighter) Rogue (think; uh.. ROGUE, duh) Accolyte (think; Cleric, Monk) Naturalist (think; Ranger, Druid, not nudity) Artificer (think; Mechanic, Engineer, Alchemist, but magic) Bard (think; Performer, Musician, Actor, Troubadour) Healer (think; Herbalist, Medieval surgeon, Doctor) 🗺️ TAVERN LOCATIONS IRL Locations: Idle Hands Brewing Co. Vladimir Caamano
 is a stand-up comedian and actor best known for his recurring roles on NBC's Superstore and Marvel's Runaways on Hulu and the CBS police drama Tommy starring opposite Edie Falco. events.title: Jake Leckie Quartet
events.description:
$20 admission / 3pm doors / 3:30 show / seated / all ages Boston born Brookline raised bassist Jake Leckie returns to his hometown to present acoustic, organic, soulful folk-jazz for his people! Jake Leckie - Bass/Compositions Noah Preminger - Saxophone Jesse Taitt - Piano Tyson Jackson - Drums 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Jake Leckie  creates organic soulful avant-groove folk-jazz for the people! With firm roots in jazz, his bass playing is informed by classical, gospel, latin, folk, & hip-hop. He has played internationally at festivals including  Newport  and  Havana Jazz , toured with  Sixto Rodriguez ,  The Harlem Gospel Travelers , and  Matthew Whittaker , and worked as a session bassist with multi-platinum Grammy award winning producer  Daniel Tannenbaum  (aka  Bekon ) on recordings for charting pop artists such as  Jessie Murph . He has performed with a diverse array of musicians including  Cat Toren ,  Hitomi Oba ,  Susan Alcorn ,  Matana Roberts ,  String Orchestra of Brooklyn ,  Vardan Ovsepian , and  Pacific Mambo Orchestra . He produced several albums, including  Chris McCarthy ’s Ropeadope release Still Time To Quit,  Sebastien Ammann 's Resilience, and mixed numerous recordings including five albums by  Thumbscrew  ( Mary Halvorson ,  Michael Formanek ,  Tomas Fujiwara ). His work as a composer can be heard on  PBS ,  BBC ,  HBO ,  CNN , and  NBC , and on the comedy-dance-sketch-fantasy  Snowy Bing Bongs Across The North Star Combat Zone .  Born in Boston, Leckie developed an interest in improvised music at a young age studying with  John Lockwood . He recorded with avant-noir pianist  Ran Blake , reggae guitarist  Lyn Taitt , and long time friends  Eli “Paperboy” Reed  and  Eli Keszler . He earned a degree in Anthropology with a concentration in Ethnomusicology from the  Johns Hopkins University  in Baltimore while studying bass with  Michael Formanek  and playing in the music ministry of a Baptist church, and a Masters in Audio Science from the Recording Arts department of the  Peabody Conservatory  where he studied with  Gary Thomas  and  Jeff Weisner , and had opportunities to perform with  George Garzone ,  Warren Wolf , and  Yo-Yo Ma . Leckie recorded his debut album  The Abode  in New York with trumpeter  Kenny Warren , pianist  Sebastien Ammann , drummer  Nathan Ellman-Bell , and guest artists  Caroline Davis ,  Daniel Prim , and  Alexis Morrast , which was released on  Outside In Music  in 2019 to critical acclaim. After relocating to LA, he produced his second album,  The Guide , an analog acoustic folk-jazz recording released on  Ropeadope Records  in 2022, with guitarist  Nadav Peled  and drummer  Beth Goodfellow . His third album of original music,  Planter of Seeds , featuring  The Guide Trio  with pianist  Cathlene Pineda , saxophonist  Randal Fisher , and trombonist  Darius Christian , was released in 2024. He now lives in Boston, MA, and is active as an artist and educator. www.jakeleckie.com

events.title: Joe Hunt Group
events.description:
$15 admission / Start 8:30pm / Doors 8pm / Seated Show Modern jazz played by Boston's best jazz musicians. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Joe Hunt  is a jazz drummer, educator, author, and historian. In the early 1960s, Joe Hunt performed and recorded alongside the late NEC Distinguished Artist-in-Residence Emeritus George Russell, with releases on Decca and Riverside. Hunt joined The Stan Getz Quartet in 1964, recording several releases on Verve, then was a member of the Bill Evans Trio from 1966-1967. The remainder of the 1960s found Hunt performing or recording with several other jazz luminaries including Chet Baker, Eric Dolphy, Dizzy Gillespie, Dexter Gordon, Charles Mingus, Bob Brookmeyer, and the late Herb Pomeroy. In the 1970s and 1980s, Hunt was a member of The National Jazz Ensemble, led jazz groups with John Scofield, Mike Stern, and Santi Debriano, and toured with quartets of Red Rodney and Hal McKusick. The 1990s, and beyond, have included membership in The Smithsonian Jazz Masters Orchestra, with former NEC president Gunther Schuller, performances with Kenny Burrell, Joe Lavano, Joanne Brackeen, and Tal Farlow, as well as recordings with the Bert Seager Quintet, and also, Trio. Hunt is the author of the 1994 book 52nd Street Beat, which is a historical look at jazz drummer greats from 1945 to 1965. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Joe Hunt quartet features a modern jazz ensemble music played by top local pros: Mark Pinto - alto saxophone, formerly years with the Buddy Rich band John Lockwood – bass, formerly with Joe Henderson, Lee Konitz, current Fringe member Yuka Hamano Hunt – piano, voice, arranger Joe Hunt – drums, formerly with George Russell, Stan Getz, Jim Hall, Dexter Gordon, and Bill Evans We pay tribute to a special composer or performer at most performances. Recent shows have included: Burt Bacharach, Ahmad Jamal, Bill Evans, and Gigi Gryce. Future shows will include the music of Paul and Carla Bley, and arranger, Johnny Mandel. - Continuing of the 3rd Sunday of Every Month

$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Special Guest , Trumpet Special Guest , Bass 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. In 1988, Boston's Pride March took to the streets with speeches, music, and voices that shaped the movement. This screening invites you to witness that moment, hear those voices, and connect with the local queer history of Boston. events.description:
$10 admission / 7pm / seated show Jesse Gallagher  began living above the Lilypad in 2006, just a few blocks from where his grandfather grew up on Inman st.  At the time Jesse was in the middle of what would be about a decade of regular touring, performing & recording with his psychedelic rock band Apollo Sunshine.  The band was featured in the New York Times, Rolling Stone, Spin & shared the stage with legendary acts  Wu-Tang Clan ,  Toots & The Maytals ,  The Flaming Lips  &  Dr. Dog . Jesse has been involved with the Lilypad for 20 years and the full time talent booking agent since 2013. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Breaking Bad used Jesse’s song “We are Born When We Die” (2008) to dramatic effect. “Today is the Day” (2005) was in international Nike commercials while his “Singing to the Earth to Thank Her For You” was used in a large GAP campaign. Gallagher has collaborated, recorded & performed extensively w/  Sam Cohen ,  Willy Mason ,  Lilys ,  Nick Nicely ,  Doug Tuttle  &  Edan . Gallagher is a certified Yoga & Meditation teacher and hosts classes at the Lilypad & online. Since 2018, he has released 40 pieces of instrumental music which have been used in millions of YouTube videos ranging from NBC NY to Tesla and most recently a string of viral videos by Emma Chamberlain. Gallagher has a very active YouTube channel, making lots of psychedelic music videos and building a community of mindful listeners. @jessegallagher.tv Steve Fell  is a guitarist, composer, and educator whose performing and recording career over the last twenty five years has reached across the boundaries of jazz, experimental, funk, free form improvisation, rock, electronic, reggae/calypso, hip-hop, psych, and many others.   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 He co-leads the groups  Clear Audience, Quantum Banditos, Dome Room,  and  Astronomico,  leads a trio under his own name, and collaborates with numerous bands and artists. @stevefellmusic

$10 admission / $5 students / 7:30 doors / 8pm start / seated Thrown Together   is a Boston based jazz collective bringing together established and emerging artists who share a passion for the tradition and ever-evolving language of jazz. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Thrown Together  is a Boston-based jazz collective bringing together exceptional established and emerging artists united by a shared passion for the tradition and ever-evolving language of jazz. The ensemble features  Eamonn Connolly  (trumpet),  Ella Xhoja  (alto saxophone),  Mark Zaleski  (alto saxophone),  Madalena Kozol  (bass), and  Bennett Frost  (drums). Connolly, Xhoja, Kozol, and Frost first performed together as members of the 2026 Cape Ann Jazz Workshop under the direction of acclaimed saxophonist  Alexa Tarantino , where they developed a musical chemistry rooted in collaboration, creativity, and improvisation. Joining them is acclaimed saxophonist, educator, and composer  Mark Zaleski , whose work as a leader and sought-after sideman has made him a prominent voice on the New England jazz scene. A faculty member at both the Berklee College of Music and the New England Conservatory, Zaleski brings years of performance experience and artistic mentorship to the ensemble. Together, Thrown Together presents fresh, engaging performances that honor jazz's storied legacy while embracing the energy and perspectives of its next generation.

$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. 
 
 
 
 
    Reserve a spot
   
 
 
 
 
 
 (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

events.title: The Quintet - Original Jazz by Eriko Yamaki
events.description:
$10 admission / 3:45 doors / 4pm start / seated & standing These works were originally composed as contemporary classical pieces and have been performed in recent years by classical musicians. For this show, the pieces have been newly arranged for jazz quintet. The music weaves together intricate and distinctive musical ideas with warm, lyrical melodies and inviting harmonies, creating a sound that is both adventurous and approachable. We anticipate that this blend of contemporary classical music and jazz will offer an engaging and memorable experience for audiences of all backgrounds. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Eriko Yamaki | Composer & Jazz Pianist Her distinct artistry has been recognized globally, earning finalist honors in prestigious international contests, including the 2018 Nosa ISAM Composition Competition with  Mysterious Bell —inspired by Haruki Murakami’s novel  Killing Commendatore —and the Kwidzyn Classical Music Competition. Eriko’s music is praised for its exceptional focus; as noted by David Kettle in  The Strad Magazine , her piano trio  "Multiple Views From a Window"  unites the violin, cello, and piano in a dense, lockdown-inspired creation of exemplary focus and intensity. Her creative reach spans from delicate flute solos to rich string orchestra pieces, with performances captivating audiences in cultural hubs such as Tokyo, Kyoto, Boston, New York, Athens, Moldova (Chișinău), and Belarus. Following pieces recorded by renowned pianist Tamara Licheli for  New Music Solo Piano , Eriko’s compositions are scheduled to be featured on her sixth album release this summer. This spring, she marked a major milestone with the highly acclaimed publication of her first score,  "Virtual"  for oboe and piano, through Austria’s historic Universal Edition. She is currently preparing a succession of upcoming works for consecutive publication with them. Looking ahead to this autumn, Eriko is set to premiere two highly anticipated works: a sonata for oboe and piano in Boston, and a brand-new piece for flute quartet and piano in Tokyo, continuing to expand her vibrant, global musical footprint. erikoyamaki.com

events.description:
$15 / $10 students / 7pm  / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Every Monday at 7PM Line-up subject to change

events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Special Guest , Trumpet Special Guest , Bass 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Continuing Every Monday at 8:30pm Lineup subject to change

events.description:

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.title: Bruce Gertz Quintet
events.description:
$15 / $10 students / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated Bruce Gerts, bass Rick DiMuzio, tenor sax Gilson Schachnik, piano Gary Fieldman, drums 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Bruce's new solo recordings are like meditations that vibrate in the solar plexus and resonate through your being. His command of the instrument and imagination are an elixir for being transported to the pure music channel. Bravo Bruce -  Jerry Bergonzi Every morning, world-renowned jazz bassist, composer, and educator, Bruce Gertz, makes himself a cup of coffee and sits at the baby grand piano of his Melrose, MA living room. Surrounded by quirky plants, records of his esteemed inspirations, and albums of his own, Gertz composes something every day, regardless of the day’s events ahead. He says, "Sometimes I only get a short idea but that can be the seed of a beautiful composition." His counterparts applaud him for his restless commitment to self-improvement. Gertz is known for his superb mastery of the upright bass and was named “Outstanding Bassist” by Boston Music Awards. What some fans don’t know is that he grew up playing electric bass from the age of 14 and still plays (and teaches) the electric quite often. His extraordinary contribution to music education has earned him multiple recognition awards from The International Association of Jazz Educators and the Jazz Education Network. He has been serving as a Professor of Bass at Berklee College of Music since 1976. Additional educator credits include serving on the advisory board of the International Society of Bassists and as an adjudicator at the Clark Terry UNH Jazzer's Festival. Gertz has performed and recorded with such artists as Gary Burton, Jerry Bergonzi, John Abercrombie, Joey Calderazzo, Kenny Werner, Mick Goodrick, Kurt Rosenwinkel, Billy Hart, Bill Frisell, Bob Berg, George Cables, Gil Evans, Tom Harrell, Jon Hendricks, Diane Schuur, Dave Brubeck, George Garzone, Mike Stern, Larry Coryell, Joe Lovano, Cab Calloway, Maynard Ferguson, Count Basie and many others. He is an author of six books and contributing editor to Bass World Magazine. As a bandleader, Gertz has recorded more than twenty albums. His latest quartet release received four stars in Downbeat, December, 2017.

events.description: Reserve your spot here Ready to meet local singles face-to-face? Join us for a fun, low-pressure evening of meaningful connections! Ditch the swiping. Come meet real, local singles in person. This is your excuse to get out, look good, grab a drink, and actually connect with people face to face. No more endless texting and never meeting in-person, no more guessing.. just a fun, social night where you can talk, laugh, flirt, and see what happens. Our speed dating events are designed to feel natural and effortless. It’s everything you wish dating apps felt like… but in real life. Note on Age Range:  While this event is geared toward the age range listed in the title, it’s not a strict rule. If you feel like you’d vibe with this crowd, you’re welcome to join. Our goal is always to create a well-balanced group where connections actually make sense. 🎟️ Ticket Pricing Reserve your spot early! Ticket prices increase once the first 20 tickets have been sold. Our events are intentionally kept at a comfortable size to ensure everyone has enough time to meet each participant. As events fill up, ticket prices increase, so we recommend reserving your spot early to lock in the best price. Don’t wait. Secure your ticket before the first 20 spots are gone! ⸻ How the Night Works Start with a Social Mixer Kick things off with a relaxed mingle. Grab a drink (not included, but highly encouraged), settle in, and get comfortable before the rounds begin. Easy, Guided Conversations We keep things flowing so you don’t have to overthink it. Each round includes a fun icebreaker, and our host guides the room so everything feels smooth, upbeat, and never awkward. Quick, Real Connections You’ll spend a few minutes with each person, just enough time to catch a vibe before rotating. It’s light, fun, and way more natural than sitting through a full date. Match the Ones You’re Into After each round, you’ll mark “friend,” “date,” or “none” on our simple matching system. If it’s mutual, we’ll send you each other’s info the next day. ⸻ A Few Things to Know ⏰ Please arrive 15–30 minutes early to check in and get settled. We start on time, and late arrivals may not be accommodated. 💡 This is meant to be fun! The best way to enjoy it is to stay open, be present, and focus on meeting new people. Some people leave with a match, others leave with new connections—either way, it’s a great night.

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Macdara Yeates Concert
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 Thursday August 27, 7pm McCarthy’s Pub Upstairs, 1920 Massachusetts Ave, Cambridge, MA (Right on Porter square) $20 for FSSGB members, $25 for non-members Macdara Yeates  is an Irish folk singer. Born and raised in Dublin, Yeates is one of a crop of artists associated with the recent resurgence of young folk talent in the Irish capital, alongside acts such as Lankum, Ye Vagabonds, and Landless. In 2012, Macdara became a founding member of The Night Before Larry Got Stretched, a monthly Dublin folk gathering, counting such luminaries as Lisa O’Neill, Ian Lynch and Radie Peat (Lankum) among its earliest attendees. Then, from 2013 to 2017, Yeates served as a member of seven-piece trad ensemble Skipper’s Alley, recording and touring across the UK, Europe, India, Canada, and the USA. Following the release of  Traditional Singing from Dublin , Macdara was nominated for two RTÉ Radio One Folk Awards, including a nomination for ‘Best Folk Singer’ alongside Ríognach Connolly, Cathy Joran and Christy Moore. With a stentorian voice described as “a bracing, baleful, baritone that sounds as if it’s been dug from the deepest, most fragrant turf” (Songlines), Macdara Yeates is ploughing his furrow as a solo performer, garnering wide critical praise and performing on some of the most coveted stages in folk music, from An Góilín Traditional Singers’ Circle to the Sidmouth Folk Festival. “Macdara Yeates is a mighty chanter.” – Christy Moore “In a golden age for traditional singing in Ireland, Yeates’s debut comes as a further welcome affirmation that the torch is being passed to a generation who truly understand and value its worth, while unafraid to inhabit it with their own particular voice.” – The Irish Times

events.description:

Geneva Rust-Orta
 is a comic and writer originally from Oakland, CA. She was named Second Funniest Jew at the 2015 Jewish Comedian of the Year Festival in London, UK. She took a half-hour comedy show to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival in 2016 and 2017 and performed another half-hour, "Gayby Girl", off-Broadway at the SoHo Playhouse in 2022 and 2023. Currently based in Brooklyn, she is a regular at the SoHo Playhouse Huron Comedy Club and was titled "Resident Sex Symbol" at Cuckoo's Open Mic. Originally from the Bay, she's performed in the Oakland Comedy Festival, Santa Cruz Comedy Festival, and SF Sketchfest.




Gabbie Watts
 is a stand-up comic based in Atlanta, GA. She’s a regular at the Laughing Skull Lounge and has brought her aggressive monotone and wry charm to Lookout Comedy Festival, Red Clay Comedy Festival, West End Comedy Fest, Flyover Comedy Festival, and Fountain City Comedy Festival. She was the winner of the 2023 “Queer of the Year” competition at the P3 Comedy Fest. Also a history buff, Gabbie hosts iHeart podcast American Filth, where she tells a filthy story from American history every week through a bisexual revisionist lens. Her comedy songs are beloved by hordes of mentally ill adults on TikTok.

Dave Fox is an accomplished, versatile drummer and is currently a full-time member of The Gravel Project, Dan Rockett and The Guilty Party and
“AS3” along with Andrew Stern and Brad Barrett.

As a sideman for over two decades, he has performed with a diverse group of artists including Jerry Bergonzi, John Lockwood, Josh Smith, Dave Tronzo, Charles Neville, Stan Strickland, The Stompers and Tom Hambridge and The Rattlesnakes to name a few.

events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

events.title: Psychedelic Soundbath w/ Jesse Gallagher
events.description:
$25 general admission / $15 students & seniors / 7:30 doors / 8pm start / lying down & seated Relax into a psychedelic world of color and sound in this Psychedelic Soundbath with Jesse Gallagher. Space is limited. 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Jesse fills the Lilypad with a live ambient soundbath along with his colorful analog projections making Lilypad’s muraled walls come to life! This show is best enjoyed lying down on a yoga mat, making yourself as comfortable as possible. Please bring a pillow, blanket, slippers or anything else to make this experience cozy. Yoga mats will be provided. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Jesse Gallagher  began living above the Lilypad in 2006, just a few blocks from where his grandfather grew up on Inman St.  At the time, Jesse was in the middle of what would be about a decade of regular touring, performing & recording with his psychedelic rock band Apollo Sunshine.  The band was featured in the New York Times, Rolling Stone, Spin & shared the stage with legendary acts  Wu-Tang Clan ,  Toots & The Maytals ,  The Flaming Lips  &  Dr. Dog . Jesse has been involved with the Lilypad for 20 years and the full time talent booking agent since 2013. Breaking Bad used Jesse’s song “We are Born When We Die” (2008) to dramatic effect. “Today is the Day” (2005) was in international Nike commercials while his ballad “Singing to the Earth to Thank Her For You” was used in a large GAP campaign. Gallagher has collaborated, recorded & performed extensively w/  Sam Cohen ,  Willy Mason ,  Lilys ,  Nick Nicely ,  Doug Tuttle  &  Edan . Gallagher is a certified Yoga & Meditation teacher and hosts classes at the Lilypad & online. Since 2018, he has released 40 pieces of instrumental music which have been used in millions of YouTube videos ranging from NBC NY to Tesla and most recently a string of viral videos by Emma Chamberlain. Gallagher has a very active YouTube channel, making lots of psychedelic music videos and building a community of mindful listeners. @jessegallagher.tv

events.title: Elan Mehler Trio
events.description:
$15 admission / $10 students / 7pm  / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

events.title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Special Guest , Trumpet Special Guest , Bass 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.title: Bert Seager's Heart of Hearing
events.description:
$15 suggested / $5 with Student ID / 6:30pm start / seated 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Bert Seager’s Heart of Hearing is a-jazz quartet made up of piano, tenor-saxophone, upright-bass, and drums whose aim is to bring listeners into the heart of improvised jazz. The joyful expression of this musical intimacy, the shimmering transparency of the sound, and the sense that these musicians are as much involved in listening as in playing makes for compelling and memorable performances.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Bert Seager , pianist, composer, recording artist, and educator, has led performances in international jazz festivals in Canada, Peru, Bulgaria, Jordan, Ecuador, Israel, China and Japan. As a composer, he is a three-time recipient of the prestigious MacDowell Colony fellowship, an artists residency program in Peterborough, New Hampshire. He has recorded 18 compact discs which have all been released internationally to critical acclaim. Cadence Magazine says Bert’s music is filled with “effervescent optimism.” And the Boston Globe wrote that his “kind of exuberance makes the jazz world go round.” 
 Rick DiMuzio , tenor saxophonist, composer, and educator, has performed concerts and clinics throughout the United States, Europe, Central and South America, and Asia. In addition to his performing career, Rick is a full Professor at Berklee College of Music where he teaches ear training, improvisation, saxophone, and ensembles. He earned his doctorate in jazz composition from New England Conservatory, a master’s degree in jazz performance from the Eastman School of Music, and a bachelor’s degree in music education from Indiana University of PA.  
 Bassist  Andrew Schiller , after living in Brooklyn NY, for five years, working as a bandleader and sideman playing jazz and improvised music, came to Boston to earn his doctorate in music from the New England Conservatory in 2020. He is now teaching at Berklee College of Music and Salem State University. Andrew’s debut album, "Tied Together, Not To The Ground," was released in May 2017, and his most recent project is "Sonoran," an 9-part suite for quintet are both on Red Piano Records. These albums feature an adventurous and unique compositional style, blending jazz with contemporary classical, rock, and avant-garde influences. 
 Dor Herskovits  is an Israeli drummer and composer based in Boston. Following his passion for jazz and improvised music, Herskovits received his Bachelor’s degree from the Berklee College of music and his Master’s degree in Jazz Performance from the New England Conservatory. During these formative years, the drummer also began his journey as a composer and bandleader. Today, Herskovits performs and records as a sideman and a bandleader around the world. His current projects include – Earprint, Tetraptych, Bert Seager, Elan Mehler trio, TJ and the Revenge, Max Ridley’s Basement Orchestra, Xiongguan Zhang, and many others. He has shared the stage with great musicians such as Jason Palmer, Steve Cardenas, Jon Cowherd, Daniel Rotem and George Garzone.

events.description: $10 admission / 7pm doors / 7:30 show / seated & standing Get Tickets Louisa Stancioff LOU-WEE-ZA STAN-CHOFF Born and raised in the foothills of Western Maine, Louisa Stancioff learned to entertain herself by singing songs with her sister and playing the piano, fiddle, guitar and any other instrument lying around the house. Stancioff grew up learning traditional Balkan music from her paternal grandfather’s side of the family, and reveled in singing American folk and roots tunes with her friends. She moved through life nomadically in her early adulthood, living in upstate New York, Western North Carolina, Montana and California, and gathered her songwriting material along the way, playing in multiple bands throughout those years. Currently settled in Midcoast Maine, she has toured this iteration of her indie folk band all across the country, headlining and opening for bands such as Blitzen Trapper, Pokey Lafarge, Darlingside, The Dead Tongues, Micaela Davis and more.   Backed by her talented bandmates, her intelligent and soulful writing pairs with a confident and catchy indie sound drawing on folk, rock, pop, and her own balkan heritage. Louisa’s debut album When We Were Looking was released in 2024 under Yep Roc Records. www.louisastancioff.net Strange Currencies by Louisa Stancioff How's About Charlie How’s About Charlie has been a New England favorite since their formation in 2016, when a sweet crew of friends became known for their soul-stirring harmonies, intimate lyrics, and magnetic stage presence. Blending acoustic textures with modern storytelling, the band crafts songs that feel both timeless and fresh, capturing the emotional complexity of love, loss, and the human experience. Whether performing in cozy living rooms or under festival lights, How’s About Charlie brings a raw honesty and warmth that draws listeners in and keeps them close. This Grammy-ballot band has performed alongside Brenda Bennett, opened for Pete Francis of Dispatch, and recently released “Sweet”, an EP recorded and produced in the heart of Nashville's Music Row. @howsaboutcharlie Sweet by How's About Charlie

events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum. Please Arrive Early to Guarantee Seating.
Born and raised in The Bronx, New York, 
Mark Viera
 became fascinated with comedy very early on. While Mark’s mom spent countless hours as a social worker to provide for her family, Mark and his older brother would pass the time watching the popular TV shows of the 70’s and 80’s. He became so engaged in the performances of his favorite comic personalities, it didn’t take long before he began to emulate the characters he came to love. On any given night, he would entertain his family with remarkably accurate portrayals from shows like “Carol Burnett”, “Sanford and Son”, and “Three’s Company”. Mark’s numerous television credits include performances on the critically acclaimed “Martin Lawrence Presents 1st Amendment Stand-Up”, “Comedy Central’s Russell Simmons Presents Stand-Up at the El Rey”, AXS TV’s “Gotham Comedy Live” a live stand up performance, BET’s “ComicView”, and Comedy Centrals “Gabriel Iglesias Presents: Stand Up Revolution”. Mark’s most recent television appearances are several episodes of Byron Allen’s “Comic Unleashed.” He was recently asked to join comic icon Gabriel Iglesias’s “Unity Through Laughter” world tour.

events.title: Hatha Yoga w/ Live Music
events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

events.title: THE SPECIFIC HEATS (record release) with ADULT LEARNERS
events.description:
$12 admission / $10 for students / 4pm doors / all ages 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Specific Heats create jangly, introspective indie pop that fuses their love for 1960s pop, garage, and surf with a dash of post-punk energy.  The group started in Boston and then were split between their hometown and Brooklyn. During that time, the band built a reputation and fan base for their energetic live performances, with consecutive summer tours in the UK and Scandinavia, and appeared in one incarnation or another for three consecutive years at the Indie Tracks festival in the UK. After a lengthy hiatus, The Specific Heats returned in 2024 with a new EP titled "Decaydes Later." As of this summer, they've officially returned home to Boston and have just released their third full-length, "Everything We Never Were (but Always Wanted to Be)," which Jangle Pop Hub calls "a triumphant return." This show is both a record release party for that album and a Boston homecoming. Featuring members of Kathy Snax and Pledge Pins, Boston's Adult Learners play ridiculously catchy, keyboard-laden power pop through a punk filter. They've just released their fantastic debut EP on Maine's Saccharine Tryst Records.

events.title: ATTIAS/DAVIS/MELA
events.description:
$20 / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated Drawing on years of criss-cross in many ballrooms, tonight will be this special trio's second dance. Don't miss it!  Michaëal Attias - Alto & C-Soprano Saxophones Francisco Mela - Drums Kris Davis - Piano 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Michaël Attias 
 has earned a reputation as one of the most questing and keenly collaborative figures on the 21st-century New York jazz scene, with a background and outlook that make him “an emphatically cosmopolitan saxophonist and composer,” according to  The New York Times . Migrations spanning North Africa, the Middle East, Western Europe and the American Midwest ultimately brought Attias to New York City in 1994, where he continues to pursue his muse as improviser, composer and  bandleader .  The Village Voice  described Attias’ music-making as, “perpetually shifting tunes, richness of timbre and a singular personality—you can almost see his music expanding and contracting.” As a leader, he has released eight  albums , including the 2019 Out Of Your Head release  échos la nuit (featuring Attias solo on alto saxophone and piano), and the 2017 Clean Feed debut of Attias’  Nerve Dance  quartet. As a sideman, he has performed and recorded alongside some of today’s most original and compelling musicians, luminaries such as Anthony Braxton, Paul Motian, Oliver Lake, Anthony Coleman, Ralph Alessi, Tony Malaby, Kris Davis, Andy Milne, Fay Victor and a host of others. In New York City, he has performed at the Village Vanguard, the Jazz Gallery, Roulette, the Stone, Dizzy’s Coca Cola, the Winter Jazz Festival and the Vision Festival – as well and in countless other festivals, clubs and performance spaces around the globe. 
 
 
 
 
 
 michaelattias.com 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Kris Davis 
 is a Grammy Award–winning pianist and composer described by The New York Times as a beacon for “deciding where to hear jazz [in New York] on a given night.” Widely recognized for her singular compositional voice, rhythmic approach, and distinctive harmonic language, Davis blends elements of jazz, groove, and contemporary classical music to create a sound that has established her as one of the most influential creative voices and collaborators in contemporary jazz. She has released 27 recordings as a leader or co-leader and has collaborated with artists including Terri Lyne Carrington, Dave Holland, John Zorn, Craig Taborn, Ingrid Laubrock, Tyshawn Sorey, and esperanza spalding. Davis was named a 2021 Doris Duke Artist and has been voted Pianist of the Year in the DownBeat Critics poll in 2020, 2022, 2025 and 2026. She serves as Associate Program Director of Creative Development at the Berklee Institute of Jazz and Gender Justice and Professor of Piano and Composition at The Musik Academie Jazzcampus in Basel, Switzerland. Davis is a Steinway Artist. 
 
 
 
 
 
 krisdavis.net 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Francisco Mela 
 was born in Bayamo, Cuba. He moved to Boston in 2000 to pursue a degree at Berklee College of Music and, quickly thereafter, the faculty recognized that Mela had much to offer students and promptly hired him to teach at the school. Mela rapidly made a name for himself on the Boston scene, becoming the house drummer at the legendary Wally’s Café Jazz Club. It was at Wally’s that Mela began developing a concept for his own band, one that would feature the sounds of modern jazz with the traditional music he grew up with in Cuba. In 2009, he was tapped by jazz legend McCoy Tyner to join his trio. Said Tyner of his new drummer, “Mela is just a fantastic player. He has his own style and his own sound, which is what I look for in a drummer.” Mela now plays every night at the Lilypad with The Fringe, and many other places around Boston.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Special Guest , Trumpet Special Guest , Bass 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Shane Torres
 is a standup comedian, writer, podcaster, and actor who resides in Brooklyn. Produced by Bert and LeeAnn Kreischer, Shane’s very first special THE BLUE EYED MEXICAN was released in December 2023. Vulture named it as one of the stand-up specials not-to-be-missed in 2023, raving “The Blue Eyed Mexican, stands out for its beautiful directness and keen sense of good storytelling. It’s a refreshing combination of delicate and obscene.” It is available to stream on YouTube. Shane can be seen on CONAN (twice), THE LATE SHOW WITH STEPHEN COLBERT, NBC’S LAST COMIC STANDING, HALF HOUR SPECIAL WITH COMEDY CENTRAL, and THIS WEEK FROM THE CELLAR on Comedy Central. You might have heard Shane’s “laconic drawling delivery with deliberate pacing” as the NY Times calls it, on popular podcasts such as BERTCAST WITH BERT KREISCHER, BARSTOOL’S KFC RADIO, DR DREW AFTER DARK, THE HONEYDEW WITH RYAN SICKLER, and ARE YOU GARBAGE and a slew of others. His podcast, NO ACCOUNTING FOR TASTE with Kyle Kinane is available wherever you get your podcasts.

events.title: Live at the Druid presents Nuala Kennedy & Alan Murray
events.description:
Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Nuala Kennedy & Alan Murray  Singing the Year Songs for the Celtic Seasons. Two current members of the Celtic Supergroup Solas combine in a beautiful intimate duo show centered around the traditional seasons of Samhain (Winter), Imbolc (Spring) Beltane (Summer) and Lúnasa (Fall). Nuala Kennedy is one of Ireland's more beloved traditional singers whose repertoire ranges from starkly powerful ancient Irish language songs to singalong ballads and thoughtful folk songs. Alan Murray is a sought-after accompanist on guitar and bouzouki who also performs songs from his native Scotland. This concert will showcase some new music inspired by the Celtic Calendar, as well as some well-known songs and tunes guaranteed to lift the spirits. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 World renowned traditional singer and flute player  Nuala Kennedy  grew up playing Irish music in Dundalk, County Louth and now lives in Ennis, County Clare with her Appalachian singer husband A. J. Roach and their two young children. Her newest release (August 2024) is an atmospheric duo album of songs recorded with Eamon O’ Leary entitled ‘Hydra’. She is a musical adventurer who is recognized world-wide as a superlative performer of traditional music. Nuala joined Solas as singer for their 30th Anniversary Reunion in 2025. She has graced the cover of Irish Music Magazine, Sing Out! and appeared on the mainstage at festivals and venues around the world including Rudolstadt (GER) Celtic Connections (UK) Milwaukee Irish festival (USA) Telemark (NOR) Eurofonik (FRA) National Folk Festival (AU) and Celtic Colors (CAN). Her discography includes several releases on Nashville’s Compass Records (USA), Vertical (UK), Borealis Records (CAN) and Ta:Lik Records (NOR) as well on her independent label Under the Arch Records (IRL). Alan Murray  is a celebrated guitarist, bouzouki player, and singer from Glasgow, Scotland, known for his powerful accompaniment style and deep roots in traditional Celtic music. He began his musical journey on the whistle before transitioning to guitar and bouzouki, quickly becoming immersed in Scotland’s rich folk traditions. After relocating to the United States, he established himself as one of the most sought-after accompanists and educators in the traditional music world. With a dynamic blend of rhythm, harmony, and sensitivity to melody, Alan has toured and recorded extensively across the globe. His impressive list of collaborators includes Solas, Lúnasa, Eileen Ivers, Battlefield Band, We Banjo 3, among many others. His ability to enhance and support traditional tunes with depth and creativity has earned him widespread respect on stages and in studios worldwide.

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. September 13: Sam Bayer Cambridge-based smartass troubadour Sam Bayer is your literate, exuberant guide to an imaginary world where housewives win the Nobel Prize in physics, poker-playing children gamble over their bedtimes, and metaphorical elephants pirouette in the den, four and a half minutes at a time. His latest studio CD, Bad Apple, brings 11 gems from his universe to yours. October 11: Terry Kitchen Called "one of New England's best songwriters" by The Boston Globe, Terry Kitchen has been performing on folk stages across the country since the 1990s, releasing a dozen albums filled with literate musical storytelling, supple guitar playing and distinctive, intimate vocals. His 2025 album We All Dream (with its title song reaching the top ten of the national Folk-DJ chart) offers a hard-won glimmer of hope just when we need it most. His songs have won the Mid-Atlantic and USA Song Contests and been runner-up in the John Lennon Song Contest, and have appeared in numerous films. In the 1980s he was the leader of the groundbreaking Boston band Loose Ties, whose experiences he recounts in his novel Next Big Thing, called "a great debut novel" by The San Francisco Book Review. "Terry Kitchen begins where Tom Waits and Elvis Costello merge and leave off."-Vance Gilbert November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

events.title: Imagine
events.description:
$10 admission / 4pm doors / 4:30 show / standing IMAGINE  is a door to longing, wonder, stillness, anger, ecstasy, love… all the feelings that exist within all of us. This performance is a place to soften, to drift, to remember something you may have forgotten. Take this invitation to surrender to the beauty of uncertainty and rawness, and to discover what can emerge when we allow ourselves to simply imagine. What if this is all a dream? And what if this dream is the truest place you've ever been? Leo Vee 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Leo is a powerful sound-sorceress. Resentful from the maltreatment she experienced growing up, he left his hometown to live in a cabin, deep in the forest. By day he sings through his flute to the wildlife. By night she creates sound-sorcery and spells; planning vengeance upon all who have hurt her. She fights to preserve her intrinsic playfulness & steadfast spirit, but every so often, darkness inevitably consumes him and he unleashes it in a cold fury; upon those who have done terrible things. JAKE RUPLINGER 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Jake Ruplinger is an Alternative Folk artist based in Boston, MA. He moved across the states from Salt Lake City, Utah, to study composition at Berklee College of Music. By drawing inspiration from personal experience, Jake’s goal is to be truthful with every word and honest with every note. Ailin  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Ailin bridges together ambient atmospheres, intimate folk acoustics, and electronic pop elements to create a space that is lush and magical. Stories, feelings, secrets, buried deep beneath, waiting to seep through lyrics and song, hoping to reach you.

 Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow. events.description: [vc_row][vc_column][ultimate_heading source="post_title" heading_tag="h1" main_heading_color="#BE1E2D" main_heading_font_family="font_family:|font_call:" main_heading_style="font-weight:bold;"][/ultimate_heading][ultimate_spacer height="10" height_on_tabs="10" height_on_tabs_portrait="10" height_on_mob_landscape="7" height_on_mob="7"][dt_fancy_separator separator_color="accent" line_thickness="3"][ultimate_spacer height="10" height_on_tabs="10" height_on_tabs_portrait="10" height_on_mob_landscape="7" height_on_mob="7"][/vc_column][/vc_row][vc_row][vc_column][dt_fancy_image image_id="27693" onclick="lightbox" width="" caption="on"][ultimate_spacer height="32" height_on_tabs="32" height_on_tabs_portrait="32" height_on_mob_landscape="28" height_on_mob="28"][vc_column_text css=""]        Learn the story of the infant abandoned on Victory Day in 1945 and his daughter's quest to find out who he was.              David Kruh, curator of “The Story of Boston’s BIG DIG” exhibit, returns to the West End Museum with a talk based on his newest book. Little Mister Victory tells the story of co-author Tina Drzal’s decades-long search for the woman who abandoned her father on VJ Day. Using cutting-edge DNA analysis and good-old-fashioned detective work (burrowing into newspaper archives, ecclesiastic, and government documents) they found the mother, along with a surprise; abandoning her newborn baby was not the most shocking act of her life.    Little Mister Victory is also a story of America from the Second World War to today, of the many people who, whether by accident, curiosity, or in the performance of their jobs, touched the life of a helpless infant who would eventually be adopted, serve our country in Vietnam, marry, and raise a family.    Additional information on the book may be found at littlemistervictory.com    Books will be available for purchase at the event.
