events.description:
$20-$25 at the door / $15 students & seniors / 12pm start  Experience the magic of a moving meditation with Integral Yoga instructor Vienna-Parashakti. This 90-minute class is appropriate for all students, from beginners to advanced yogis. Dress comfortably, and bring a cozy blanket if you’d like. (cash or venmo accepted at the door) 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Prepare to relax and rejuvenate your body, mind, and spirit in this peaceful yoga class. Explore the guided practice of Hatha Yoga and experience a series of classical Yoga asanas (physical postures), pranayama (breath control), Yoga Nidra (deep relaxation) and meditation.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Parashakti  (Vienna) is an Integral Yoga instructor and a new-ish resident to Cambridge from two and a half years studying and teaching at  Satchidananda Ashram  in Yogaville, Virginia.  She is currently teaching weekly Hatha Yoga classes at the Lilypad and other places around Cambridge. 
 
 
 
 
 
 Musical accompaniment on the Grand Piano provided by Jesse Gallagher, along with selections from his meditation album "The Inner Sound." 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 “ It was such a delight to attend your class.  My nervous system has been a wreck and it was wonderful to be in a place that felt safe for my body.  I haven’t moved my “yogi” body in years and it felt so good to wake up the cobwebs. Thank you for providing such a beautiful space for me in a day that I really needed it. ” 
 
 — Maria 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Yoga Classes at Lilypad continue weekly on Saturdays.

events.description: Toad Revival Series — Saturdays, 4–7 PM  Every Saturday from 4 to 7, we rewind the clock and let the old sparks fly. The  Toad Revival Series  is our tribute to the bands that built this stage, note by note, night after night. It’s a laid-back, early evening show filled with familiar sounds, longtime favorites, and the spirit of a scene that never really faded—just waited for the right time to plug back in. These are the artists who gave Toad its heartbeat, returning for intimate, no-frills sets that remind us why we’re here. Think front-porch energy with barroom volume, old songs with new life, and a crowd that knows when to sing along. Come early. Stay as long as you like. This is Toad, the way it was—and still is.

events.title: TCS presents: Josh Gondelman
events.description:
18+ w/ 2-Item Suggested Minimum.




Josh Gondelman
 is a writer and comedian who incubated in Boston before moving to New York City, where he currently lives and most recently worked as the head writer and an executive producer for 
Desus & Mero 
on Showtime. Previously, he spent five years at 
Last Week Tonight with John Oliver
, first as a web producer and then as a staff writer, where he earned four Emmy Awards, two Peabody Awards, and three WGA Awards. Josh also previously wrote for Fuse TV’s 
Billy On The Street
. His most recent hour, 
Positive Reinforcement
, is now available to stream. Josh’s debut stand-up special, 
People Pleaser, 
was released in 2022. In 2016, Josh made his late-night standup debut on 
Conan 
(TBS), and he has also performed on 
Late Night With Seth Meyers 
(NBC) and 
The Late Late Show with James Corden 
(CBS). Gondelman is the author of the essay collection 
Nice Try: Stories of Best Intentions and Mixed Results, 
published in September 2019 by Harper Perennial. Since 2019, he has been a regular panelist on NPR mainstay 
Wait Wait Don’t Tell Me
. Offstage, Gondelman is also the co-author (along with Joe Berkowitz) of the book 
You Blew It
, 
published in October 2015 by Plume. His writing has also appeared in prestigious publications such as McSweeney’s Internet Tendency, New York Magazine, and The New Yorker.

events.description:
$10 advance / $12 day of show / $8 student / 5pm doors/ 5:30 show / seated An intimate early evening set from JOURNEYGLO, featuring original songs performed with special guest Micah Yoo on acoustic guitar, plus a few collaborative moments. 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 JOURNEYGLO  is a Dallas-based singer-songwriter creating intimate indie folk-pop with cinematic, ambient sensibilities. Her debut album,  Limp By Your Side , explores grief, faith, love, and the unresolved spaces between what was and what might be. For this stripped-down acoustic set, JOURNEYGLO brings the songs into a more vulnerable setting, centered on voice, guitar, haunting melodies, and honest storytelling that feels like sitting beside someone in the dark without rushing them toward resolution.   journeyglo.co @journeyglo  on instagram @journeyglo  on TikTok 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Micah Yoo 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A classical violinist by training, a songwriter by hobby, and a licensed music therapist God willing — Micah Yoo is best described as an overall music enthusiast. Having taken an extended break from both writing and performing, Micah is excited to return to the stage alongside JOURNEYGLO and rediscover the joy of sharing music with a live audience.

events.title: UPSTAIRS SHOW: Ordinary Elephant
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 "...their intimate songs, the weaving harmonies, and the stories that draw you in as if you were gathered around an enchanted campfire." - Eliza Gilkyson Mesmerizing folk duo Ordinary Elephant has spent the better part of the last decade on a never-ending tour that’s earned married couple Crystal and Pete Damore widespread critical acclaim and made fans of luminaries like Tom Paxton and Mary Gauthier. In 2017, the pair took home the International Folk Music Award for Artist of the Year on the strength of their breakout album, Before I Go, and two years later, they returned with the similarly lauded Honest, which the Associated Press hailed as “one of the best Americana albums of the year.” The band’s new stripped-down, self-titled collection is the purest distillation of their sound yet, showcasing the arresting power of the couple’s gorgeous harmonies and intricate fretwork. The songs are timeless, rooted in rich, character-driven storytelling, and the performances are similarly transportive, fueled by delicately intertwined banjo, guitar, and octave mandolin. Though the songs were born out of a period of deep uncertainty, the record itself is a work of profound self-assurance, one delivered by a duo whose personal and professional lives embody the limitless possibility of honest, organic collaboration. Press play on Ordinary Elephant and you’ll hear more than just a husband and wife; you’ll hear the sound of sincerity and commitment, of patience and gratitude, of learning to let go of expectation and revel in the simple beauty of the moment. https://www.ordinaryelephant.net/ $20 in advance. $25 at the  door.  Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang. As co-leader of Earprint, he received critical acclaim from publications such as Downbeat magazine, NPR’s critics' poll and many more.  www.dorherskovits.com

$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Special Guest , Trumpet Special Guest , Bass 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow.  Elan Mehler  has released 11 albums as a leader, with such musicians as Bill Frisell, Dave Douglas, Becca Stevens, Scott Robinson, Francisco Mela and many more and has garnered stellar reviews from such publications as The New York Times, The Guardian, Jazz Times, and Downbeat.  His latest record is a solo piano record released on Sunnyside Records that has garnered significant press.  Elan has brought his projects to clubs and festivals worldwide including Birdland, Queen Elizabeth Hall, and the North Sea Festival.  In 2016 Elan co-founded the label Newvelle Records, as artistic director of the label he has signed and produced over 50 records by artists such as Jack DeJohnette, John Patitucci, Dave Liebman, Lionel Loueke, Irma Thomas and Ellis Marsalis.  Reviews and music available at  www.elanmehler.com Max Ridley  is one of the most in-demand bassists in the Boston area. He was awarded full-tuition scholarships to study at Berklee College of Music for both undergraduate and graduate degrees, earning his graduate degree from the extremely exclusive Berklee Global Jazz Institute under the direction of master pianist, educator and humanitarian Danilo Perez. An equally important part of his education was down the street from Berklee at Boston’s historic Wally’s Jazz Cafe. He began going to jam sessions there in high school and eventually became the house bass player every Friday and Saturday night. Ridley has played and recorded with renowned musicians of many different styles all over the world.  An incredibly versatile multi-instrumentalist, Max performs regularly in bands playing Jazz, Rock, Folk, Soul, Punk, Klezmer, Polka and every other style you can think of.  He also serves as the music director for tap dance company Subject:Matter ( https://www.subjectmattertap.com/ ) and teaches music as a guest lecturer at different colleges around New England (such as Longy School of Music, University of New Hampshire and Berklee College of Music). Boston based Israeli drummer  Dor Herskovits  is already a staple of the Boston jazz scene and has won international acclaim as an improviser. His melodic approach to playing the drums, combined with vast knowledge of rhythm and a composer's vision make him a unique voice as a drummer. Dor's original music reflects the eclectic nature of music nowadays,  drawing from jazz and blues roots, folk and world music, free jazz rock and metal.   As a sought after sideman, he plays in various jazz and experimental groups on the Boston-New York line. He has also toured around the US, Canada, Europe and China. Herskovits has recorded many albums as a sideman, featured on labels such as Newvelle and Endectomorph music, alongside musicians such Grammy award-winning guitarist Bill Frisell, Michael Blake and Jason Palmer. He has also performed with George Garzone, Noah Preminger, Jon Cowherd, Steve Cardenas,Bert Seager’s Tet-rap-tych, Max Ridley’s Basement Philharmonic, Daniel Rotem and Xiongguan Zhang.  A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Comedian Bobcat Goldthwait first appeared on the David
Letterman Show at the age of 20 and has an ongoing career as a
writer, director, actor, voice actor, and stand-up. As a comedian,
Bobcat has starred in numerous HBO/Showtime specials,
performed in venues worldwide, and even went on tour as an
opening act for the band Nirvana. Well-known for his roles in
“Scrooged” with Bill Murray and as Zed in the “Police Academy”
franchise, Goldthwait has become a well-respected Award-
Winning Director, too. His directorial works include feature films
World’s Greatest Dad, starring Robin Williams, Willow Creek,
starring Bigfoot, God Bless America, Windy City Heat, Sleeping
Dogs Lie, and the documentaries Call Me Lucky and Joy Ride. In
addition to being a 4x Sundance Alumni, Goldthwait’s films have played internationally,
including the Deauville Film Festival and San Sebastian Film Festival. Bobcat has been
honored with the German Independent Honorary Award at the Oldenburg Film Festival for
his collective works and was awarded “Filmmaker on the Edge” at the Provincetown Film
Festival by his hero John Waters. His TV direction includes his series, Misfits and Monsters,
Jimmy Kimmel Live, Community, Maron, Those Who Can’t, and many more. Goldthwait has
directed numerous standup comedy specials for folks like Patton Oswalt, Marc Maron, Ron
Funches, Kyle Kinane, Cameron Esposito, Mo Willems, Gary Gulman, Hari Kondabolu,
Eugene Mirman, and Pete Davidson to name a few. Bobcat is currently working on several
new film projects and has started his autobiography.

events.title: Anna May
events.description:
Alternative tragic Americana, invocations for peace & judgment reshaping with bleeding heart stream of consciousness poems. The deep exploration of heartbreak and trauma has been an ongoing quest throughout Anna's work. Her lyrics have been heavily textured by a lonesome whimsicality that finds itself most at home in the vastness of the American West or in landscapes of stark frontiers. Anna's music honors the nomadic spirit with memory, meditation & fresh interpretations of folk music & jazz influence. She honors a hope to enhance connection, humility, healing, and joy among people in the process of parting with typical genre rules. Anna's lyrical sensibility is steeped in wisdom, and layered with evocative musicality and metaphysical embroidery while eschewing the mainstream & parting with platitudes. Anna explores both estrangement and connection while taking cues from artists like Billie Holiday, Shawn Colvin, & Neil Young. Anna has been compared to artists like Jeff Buckley & Aimee Mann. Anna has opened for artists like Kacy Hill, Amythyst Kiah, The Arcadian Wild, People Museum, & Jann Klose.

Anna has performed at wildflower music & arts festival, treefort music festival, Brick and Mortar Music Hall in San Francisco, High Dive in Seattle, the Mint in Los Angeles, Spiderhouse Ballroom in Austin, Rockwood Music Hall in New York City, Larimer Lounge in Denver, PNC Live Studio, & many more. 
Anna has been featured in publications like V13 media, WFMU, Medium, Northern Public Radio, & many more. Anna May was nominated for best Indie song of 2023 by Indie Boulevard Magazine. In 2024, Anna was a featured guest on NPR's Great American Folk Show, on WKU PBS Lost River Sessions (episode to air in 2025) & her song, The Show was chosen as song of the day on KUTX in Austin in 2024. In 2024, Anna was nominated for Best Americana Act at the New England Music Awards & was featured on the WDVX Blue Plate Special.

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. October 11: Terry Kitchen Called "one of New England's best songwriters" by The Boston Globe, Terry Kitchen has been performing on folk stages across the country since the 1990s, releasing a dozen albums filled with literate musical storytelling, supple guitar playing and distinctive, intimate vocals. His 2025 album We All Dream (with its title song reaching the top ten of the national Folk-DJ chart) offers a hard-won glimmer of hope just when we need it most. His songs have won the Mid-Atlantic and USA Song Contests and been runner-up in the John Lennon Song Contest, and have appeared in numerous films. In the 1980s he was the leader of the groundbreaking Boston band Loose Ties, whose experiences he recounts in his novel Next Big Thing, called "a great debut novel" by The San Francisco Book Review. "Terry Kitchen begins where Tom Waits and Elvis Costello merge and leave off."-Vance Gilbert November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - The Dennis Brennan Band
events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

events.title: Nondualism Trio presents Nosferatu Funk
events.description:
$15 admission / 7pm doors / 7:30 start / seated & standing The Boston-based progressive jazz group  Nondualism Trio   presents "Nosferatu Funk"  at the Lilypad! Featuring Mark Tipton (trumpet), James Heazlewood-Dale (bass), and Paul July Joseph (drums), Nondualism Trio will be playing original works, including Mark's compositions from their upcoming album, "Nosferatu Funk." The set will include: "Paraconsistent Refractions," "Walk-A-Seven Ghost Dance," "Lithospheric Waltz," "Cosmic Dust Groove Thang," "Into the Wilderness," "Slow Burn," "Nosferatu Funk," a pair of musical "Mantras," and more! Expect deep grooves, musical complexity, and synergistic ensemble playing.    
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Nondualism Trio  is a Boston-based progressive jazz trio that includes Mark Tipton on trumpet, James Heazlewood-Dale on bass, and Paul July Joseph on drums. Mark is originally from Maine, James is originally from Australia, and Paul is from Haiti. Nondualism Trio was formed in 2025 and in February 2026 they recorded their first album at Q Division Studios in Cambridge, MA, featuring Mark’s original compositions. They have recently performed at The Lilypad in Cambridge, The Drake in Amherst, and NEC’s Pierce Hall. The ensemble’s name, Nondualism Trio, is derived from the Indian philosophy that views reality as an interconnected whole, devoid of dualistic thinking, whereby awareness can be experienced beyond conceptual thought. It is this state of mind that Nondualism Trio seeks to embody when they are performing together: collectively open-minded in their improvisations to carry the music wherever it wants to go, and free from judgements and intuited mental road-blocks. Their music is both structured and open. The three members of Nondualism Trio are all rising talents in jazz, and are all active musicians on the Boston scene, seasoned touring musicians, and devoted teachers (Mark at NEC, James at Brandeis, and Paul through his private studio). James and Mark have recently toured Turkey, Cypress, and the Northeastern US with Mehmet Ali Sanlıkol and both his jazz quintet and classical Turkish music ensemble, DÜNYA, while Paul and Mark have recently toured New England. They enjoy connecting with diverse audiences and inspiring young musicians. Mark Tipton  is a Boston-based jazz trumpeter, composer, and educator who has recently been appointed as Assistant Chair of Jazz Studies at NEC. He has recently performed and/or recorded with Jerry Bergonzi, Dave Holland, Antonio Sanchez, Eguie Castrillo, Jason Moran, Allan Chase, Edmar Colón, Diego Figueiredo, Joe Hunt, Ayn Inserto, Tom Varner, and Mehmet Sanlikol. His Boston-based jazz octet released its debut album Vernacular Stretch in December 2025 at Soapbox Gallery in Brooklyn, and his progressive jazz group Nondualism Trio recorded their debut album in February 2026, featuring Mark on trumpet, James Heazlewood-Dale on bass, and Paul July Joseph on drums. Mark has toured the US, Europe, Turkey, and Cypress with numerous ensembles, and he holds a DMA degree from NEC. He enjoys sharing the joys of creative improvisation with students and audiences of all ages. James Heazlewood-Dale  is a Grammy-nominated bassist and a professor at Brandeis University, where he lectures on film music and video game history. Originally from Sydney, Australia, he moved to Boston to pursue studies in jazz double bass at Berklee College of Music and the New England Conservatory, where he received full scholarships. Dr. Heazlewood-Dale has shared the stage with world-renowned artists, including Jacob Collier, Maria Schneider, Grace Kelly, Terence Blanchard, Zakir Hussain, and Mehmet Ali Sanlıkol. He has presented at esteemed national conferences, including those for the American Musicological Society, the Musicological Society of Australia, the Jazz Education Network, and the College Music Society. Notably, he was commissioned by Decca Records to craft the liner notes for the soundtrack release of The Callisto Protocol (2022) and featured as a scholarly guest in Adam Neely's acclaimed video essay "The Nintendo-fication of Jazz." Drummer  Paul July Joseph  is from Port-au-Prince, Haiti, and is currently studying Contemporary Musical Arts at the New England Conservatory of Music. He recently won a major award from the Percussive Arts Society, and has competed in Drumfest, Le Batteur, and Drum-Off Global. He has worked with Silkroad’s Global Musician Workshop, has performed at the Panama Jazz Festival, and recently joined Akili Jamal Haynes and World of Chibuzo for a performance at Carnegie Hall, sponsored by the United Nations. His drum teachers have included Prosper Prevoit, Austin MacMahon, and Obed Calvaire. Paul is currently working on a project, Creole Jazz Fusion, which blends Haitian folk styles such as Yanvalou, Congo, Ibo, Kompa, and Zouk with jazz. He performs regularly with ensembles led by Itay Dayan, Sam Saomek Srithongkum, and Mark Tipton.   www.marktiptonmusic.com   facebook.com/markalantipton @mark.tipton.music

Sam Miller
 is a nationally touring comedian from Olympia, Washington. He is 6 foot 6, 360 pounds, has two kids, (one of them is on purpose) he's been married for 15 years, and has been clean and sober for 17 years. Sam likes to make jokes about what it's like to be a sober parent. He also likes to make jokes about what jails like in Yakima. His first album and special, Round Trip, was recorded and filmed under the tutelage of Grammy-winning producer Dan Schlissel, whose indie label, Stand Up! Records, Sam had recently signed a three-album deal with. Round Trip was released October 27th 2023 and immediately went to number one on the iTunes Comedy Charts. It even broke into the top 200 overall charts. Sam is a recurring guest and has been heard by an estimated 2.5 million listeners on the nationally syndicated "Bob & Tom Radio Show." He has written for Newsweek. He was the runner-up in the 2021 Seattle International Comedy Competition and won the Comedy on Trial Competition in 2017. He has headlined multiple major comedy clubs including Sidesplitters in Tampa, Helium in Portland, and The Laugh Factory and Zanies in Chicago. He's also performed with the Addicts Comedy Tour and at NA and AA conventions all over the country. For three consecutive years, he won awards in "The Best of Olympia" issue of the Weekly Volcano.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

events.title: Lafayette Gilchrist ft. Cecil Brooks of the Sun Ra Arkestra
events.description:
$25 at the door / $20 in advance / $15 students and seniors / 7:30 doors / seated 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist featuring special guest and Cambridge native, Cecil Brooks of the Sun Ra Arkestra. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Lafayette Gilchrist’s music draws on the span of jazz history from stride to free improvisation, along with inspiration from hip-hop, funk, and Washington D.C.’s unique go-go sound. His work thrives on making surprising connections between styles and influences, boldly veering from piledriver funk to piquant stride, vigorous swing to hip-hop swagger, contemplative abstraction to deep-bottom grooves. Gilchrist is the pianist in the Sun Ra Arkestra, has toured extensively with David Murray, and his compositions have graced the soundtracks of David Simon’s acclaimed series The Wire, The Deuce, and Treme. Gilchrist has performed with Cassandra Wilson, Macy Gray, Oliver Lake, Andrew Cyrille, Orrin Evans, Paul Dunmall, Hamid Drake, William Parker and many more. Gilchrist’s second solo recording, 2019 “Dark Matter” which muses on the elusive and mysterious matter that ties the universe together, landed on numerous critics best of lists. Gilchrist returns to The Lilypad, where he played for a standing room only crowd in 2022, for a performance featuring a special guest appearance by Cambridge native and fellow member of the Sun Ra Arkestra, Cecil Brooks on trumpet. www.lafayettegilchrist.com

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. November 8: Rachel Marie Rachel Marie (she/they) follows in a tradition of unapologetically forthright femme folksingers, with songs that hearken to "overstuffed lines of Tori Amos, philosophical turn of Indigo Girls, and lilting vocals like Joni Mitchell" (Victoria Farmer, The Christian Humanist Podcast). The social awareness of folk meets the introspection and healing of the singer-songwriter tradition, featuring the emotional catharsis and dynamic vocals of a Broadway show. With a songwriting approach as raw and honest as it's always been, Rachel Marie is making a return to live performance after an unintentional hibernation hiatus, ready to reconnect with a real live audience. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

events.description: Toad Revival Series — Saturdays, 4–7 PM  Every Saturday from 4 to 7, we rewind the clock and let the old sparks fly. events.title: Chuck Clough
events.description:
A Boston area singer/guitarist, Chuck primarily performs solo but also plays out with his band, The Butler Frogs. He has opened for touring bands America, The Wallflowers, and The Gin Blossoms. In 2020, The Butler Frogs released their sole EP, Last Call For Opinions.

He was also a founding member of Northern Point (2005-2010), an acoustic trio from the NY/NJ area that released three albums (November, Northern Point: Live at St. James' Gate, and After The Frost). 

In 2016, Chuck founded and hosted (with musician Ronnie Hirschberg) the award-winning podcast Above The Basement - Boston Music and Conversation, which won a 202o Boston Music Award for Podcast/Radio Show of the Year.  After 200 episodes, Chuck shuttered the podcast and set out on his solo musical endeavor. 

 He currently performs in New England and is always on the lookout for the lost songs that have influenced him over the years.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - The Dennis Brennan Band
events.description: Dennis Brennan was born on the wrong side of the tracks in Marlboro, Massachusetts. At age 9 he entered show business as Rumplestiltsken in a grammar school play. In 7th grade he performed “Louie Louie” with a local garage band at the Berlin, Ma. Town Hall and quickly evolved into “the lead singer” That band evolved into “The Paranoids”, his musical outlet throughout his high school years. They opened shows for both The Remains and The Barbarians, garage band legends who are each featured on “Nuggets, original artyfacts from the first psychedelic era” Rhino R2 75486. Following high school. Brennan’s education continued as lead singer in such well regarded outfits as “The Dirty Rye Band”, The West Side Band”, “The Martells”, and “Push Push”. These bands performed in every bar and dive on the east coast. An education indeed. In 1992 he formed the Dennis Brennan Band and started his solo career, quickly releasing two critically acclaimed recordings on Upstart Records, a division of Rounder. In 2000 he released “Rule #1” on ESCA Records which resulted in glowing reviews from The New Yorker, The Chicago Sun Times, The Boston Phoenix as well as other publications nationwide. These recordings showcase Brennans ability “to not just tip toes into genres, he strips naked and plunges right in.” Bill Holmes, AMPLIFIER.

events.title: Toad Sunday Revival - Tim Gearan Band
events.description: A beloved fixture in the Boston music scene for over 25 years, Tim Gearan has become a bonafide local music hero. His warm, raspy baritone, jaw-dropping guitar skills and wry, poignant songwriting have graced the bars, pubs, and music halls throughout New England and beyond, creating a loyal cult-like following. Gearan, a New York native, spent ten years touring the globe as a sideman for the great Toni Lynn Washington, as well as collaborating with Grammy-winning singer/guitarist Susan Tedeschi. Finding his own artistic voice, Gearan  has crafted an intoxicating blend of Americana, folk and blues with shades of Randy Newman, Tom Waits, JJ Cale,  Leon Russell and Lowell George. He quickly established himself as a force in the Boston’s resurgent roots music scene, and his Boston area residencies have become a “can’t miss” staple of the city’s nightlife. Gearan has released 7 albums to date, as well as 4 single releases; “While the World Goes By” (2019)  “It’s Not the End of the World"  (2019) “Hey, Hey, Hey” (2020) and “Talk About Heaven” (2020).

events.title: UPSTAIRS: Somerville Songwriter Sessions
events.description:
Learn more / Buy Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 As it has for more than a decade, Somerville Songwriter Sessions presents the finest acoustic singer-songwriters each month in an intimate, welcoming setting. Each concert features three songwriters each doing a solo set, and then trading songs in the round, allowing for stories, impromptu harmonies, jamming, and spontaneous inspiration. Each show, one of our five hosts – Rachel Marie, Terry Kitchen, Sam Bayer, Beth DeSombre, Jack Byrne – are joined by some of the best local and touring singer-songwriters on the scene. December 13: Beth DeSombre Beth DeSombre writes songs that are "smart and  uplifting...focusing on the quiet meaning to be found in ordinary life" (Sing Out! Magazine), exploring issues from the personal to the political. Her music touches both mind and heart, with insights wrapped in melody and harmony that stay with you after the echoes of the last chorus have faded away. Her newest CD Holding the Threads (2024) is her most personal album to date, telling stories about family and crisis and trying to find hope in dark times. Her previous EP The Sea Beside Us (2023), tells stories of ships and the ocean. Her 2017 EP Resistance, which was written in response to the political situation after the 2016 election, is a fundraiser for the ACLU. An award-winning writer in many formats, she has published 8 books. $15 in advance. (+ processing fees) $20 at the door. This Is An All Ages Show Doors are at 3:30pm. Showtime is 4pm. Dinner and drinks available at all tables. NO REFUNDS OR EXCHANGES

Enter our comedy world, whether you listen, laugh, bomb, groan, clap or just sip your beverage with a raised eyebrow… We just LOVE it. It’s an Open Mic, but there’s always some pros dropping in to test new material, so it’s unavoidable to have a good time, for free no less. Doors open at 6 pm. The heat starts around 7 pm.

events.title: Orkest
events.description:
Founded in 2022 by Sapphire Skye Toth and Michael Gehman while they earned their Master of Science degrees in Arts Administration at Boston University, Orkest is meant to be the place where New Music meets The Community and The Community meets New Music.

Orkest, a visionary musical venture rooted in the bustling city of Boston, is on a mission to redefine the local music scene. Recognizing the abundance of untapped musical talent, Orkest seeks to bridge the gap between emerging composers and the community, breaking away from classical traditions and creating an inviting space for diverse genres. Departing from conventional models, Orkest utilizes venues to bring people to music, not just vice versa, fostering a casual environment in cafe bars and libraries. With a commitment to equitable treatment of artists, creating opportunities for artists at socioeconomic disadvantages, professional recordings of performances, and a unique pay-what-you-wish model, Orkest is not just a music experience; it's a transformative force shaping how communities engage with and appreciate new music and the artists who create it.

 is a comedian based in New York, by way of New Orleans.  (2010),

The Half Hour

 (2014, 2015), 
The Meltdown with Jonah and Kumail 
(2015), 
This Is Not Happening
 (2015, 2017, 2019), Showtime's 
Live from SXSW 
(2017), TruTv's 
Comedy Knockout
 (2016, 2017, 2018), and

events.description: Bill Jones, a native of Marion, Massachusetts, is a tenor and soprano saxophonist that been a regular on the jazz scene since he moved to Boston in 1999 to study at the New England Conservatory. He is inspired by such greats as Joe Henderson, John Coltrane, Hank Mobley, Wayne Shorter, and Charlie Parker, as well as modern masters like Jerry Bergonzi, George Garzone, Joe Lovano, Joshua Redman, and Mark Turner. Bill regularly plays at venues in and around Boston, such as Wally’s, The Beehive, Monkfish, and Lilypad. He enjoys playing classic and modern jazz standards and his original compositions. He has performed with many revered jazz musicians, such as Bob Gullotti, Leo Genovese, Herb Pomeroy, Jeff Galindo, Tim Ray, Greg Hopkins, and John Lockwood.

events.title: JAZZ NIGHT: Dave Fox Trio
events.description:
The Dave Fox Trio is a Modern Jazz Trio featuring original jazz
compositions and arrangements inspired by artists such as John Coltrane, Joe Henderson, Chick Corea, Steve Swallow, Charles Mingus, Thelonious Monk and Wayne Shorter. The group features internationally acclaimed bassist John Lockwood and innovative Boston area musicians and composers such as guitarist Phil Sargent and saxophonists Nicholas Brust and Bill Jones.

Dave Fox is an accomplished, versatile drummer and is currently a full-time member of The Gravel Project, Dan Rockett and The Guilty Party and
“AS3” along with Andrew Stern and Brad Barrett.

As a sideman for over two decades, he has performed with a diverse group of artists including Jerry Bergonzi, John Lockwood, Josh Smith, Dave Tronzo, Charles Neville, Stan Strickland, The Stompers and Tom Hambridge and The Rattlesnakes to name a few.

past_events.description:
$10 advance / $15 at the door / 7:30 doors / 7:45 start / seated 
 
 
 
 
    Get Tickets
   
 
 
 
 
 
 Sean O’Reilly  is an indie folk-pop singer-songwriter whose music blends earthy storytelling with baroque instrumentation and dramatic vocal delivery.  Having cut his teeth in pianobars entertaining crowds for grueling multiple hour gigs with nothing more than a piano and a microphone, O’Reilly is a seasoned performer both on his own or working with other musicians and has played many of the most prestigious venues in Connecticut and is now bringing his live show to Massachusetts.   A self-taught harpist, pianist, producer, and mixer, O’Reilly’s latest EP, One Thread, was entirely produced, mixed, and mastered in his home studio—resulting in a lush, emotionally rich sound.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 @seanoreillysongs www.seanoreillyband.com

Hailing from the rugged yet loveable city of Worcester, MA, Tasteless Jack is an acoustic act from brainchild guitarist Jorge Ramirez, accompanied by cellist Skip Von Kuske, and drummer Matt Greene, all of whom share a universal passion for music.
Their songs range in a variety of styles, from soft fingerpicking in the vein of Iron & Wine, and the strong, passionate wails of Pearl Jam, to the intricate strumming patterns of Dave Matthews, their music composition isn’t beholden to any specific genre. Hence the name, “Tasteless Jack”. Tasteless Jack was nominated for best Male Vocalist at the 2025 Worcester Magazine Music Awards, he is a member of the Dirty Gerund Poetry Show house band where he performs regularly on Monday nights, and he regularly performs and hosts musicians third Wednesdays nights at Hotel Vernon for his Tasty Tunes series. His single “Weather” is currently out on Spotify and Apple Music!

past_events.title: Three Points of Note with Tyler, Sylvia, and Vince
past_events.description:
$15 admission / $10 advance / 7:15 doors / seated Three friends and each of their bands celebrate their time at Berklee in a final performance before going their separate ways. Tyler, Sylvia, and Vince each have incredibly unique and distinct musical voices, but each share a common sense of wonder and joy in the process and community of live, improvised, and exciting music. Tyler’s NEW! Quintet 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Tyler’s NEW! Quintet explores the intersections between free improvisation, Appalachian old-time music, and straight-ahead jazz. Presenting a mix of original and traditional music, the chordless quintet puts on a creative, one-of-a-kind show which never fails to surprise and intrigue. Tyler White - baritone and melody saxophones Jin Lee - alto saxophone Vince LaRosa - trombone Chase Behar - upright bass Ben Fig - drums 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Small Song 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Small Song is a band fronted by Sylvia Khouri featuring Althea Wincek, Tyler White and Julian Pavone. They blend Free Jazz, Prog Rock and Ambient sounds; Sylvia singing and playing the trumpet in non-traditional ways through a pedal board, Althea on synth sounds, June on Guitar and pedals, Julian on Drums, and Tyler on C-melody and Baritone sax. While formed at Berklee, the graduates still play together and continue to perform around Boston as well as record their debut album. The band also splits their public performances between original songs and free-improv sets to Shel Silverstein poems. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Vince LaRosa 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Vince LaRosa  sets sail into the next chapter of his musical journey with a performance branded by his own name. Being influenced by genres ranging from Motown to indie video game scores, Vince dances with the echoes of his past and the ever-changing tides of the present to shed a light on the slippery nature of identity and ’the self’. Backed by friends and collaborators David Jaques on trumpet, Devin Thai on keys, Nathan Hough on bass, and Quinn Domena on kit, Vince attempts to embark on an exploration of his- and subsequently, our own, inner world in a characteristically raw and explosive 45 minutes of music.

past_events.title: Jerry Bergonzi Quartet
past_events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 8:30 start / 8pm doors / seated  Jerry Bergonzi , Tenor Saxophone Luther Gray , Drums Special Guest , Trumpet Special Guest , Bass 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 A fine, high-powered tenor saxophonist with a tone influenced by John Coltrane, a mastery of chord changes, and a strong musical imagination,  Jerry Bergonzi  has long had an underground following in the Boston area. He started on clarinet when he was eight, switching to alto at 12, and finally to tenor two years later. Bergonzi was inspired early on by Sonny Rollins, Coltrane, and Hank Mobley. He attended Lowell University and then after graduation played electric bass in local bands behind singers and strippers, saving up enough money to move to New York in 1972. After struggling in the Big Apple for seven years and gaining some recognition as a member of Two Generations of Brubeck and of the Dave Brubeck Quartet (with whom he appeared on several Concord albums during 1979-1981), Bergonzi moved back to Boston in 1981, where he developed a strong career both as a tenorman and as an educator. He has since led several groups (including two called Con Brio and Gonz) and recorded for the Plug, Not Fat, Red, and Blue Note labels. —  By Scott Yanow, AllMusic

past_events.title: The Fringe
past_events.description:
$15 @ the door / $10 students / 10pm doors / 10:30 start / seated  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 The Fringe  originally formed back in 1971 by tenor-saxophonist  George Garzone , bassist Richard Appleman, and drummer Bob Gullotti as an outlet for their free jazz improvisations, The Fringe have entertained and enlightened Boston area jazz audiences for over 50 years. Bassist Appleman left the band in 1985 to become Chairman of the Bass Department at Berklee College and was replaced by veteran bassist  John Lockwood . Bob Gullotti passed away in 2020 and is remembered as one of the greatest jazz drummers of his generation. Francisco Mela, now on drums,  graciously fills the space Bob left behind. Along with their impressive tenure with The Fringe, Garzone, Lockwood, and Mela are in great demand as session players and have played with many of the greats of contemporary jazz. Along with keeping up with a busy performance schedule, each of them are well-respected educators helping to inspire the jazz musicians of tomorrow.
